title: OpenSSH Rushes Patches for ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass
description: A high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158) affects OpenSSH servers on Linux distributions using musl libc without PAM enabled. The flaw allows attackers to log in to certain accounts by supplying any password between 257 and 1024 characters. This impacts accounts with a password field set to "*" (no password) and requires the presence of at least one local account with a SHA-256 or SHA-512 hashed password. The vulnerability is present in Alpine Linux releases 3.16 through 3.24 and edge, among others. OpenSSH 10.6p2 includes patches to fix this issue. Immediate patching or disabling password authentication is recommended to mitigate risk.
